notes: Hello! (basic 해요체 greeting)
I'm Han. I'm in marketing starting today. (clean 해요체 self-intro)
How do I do this, 선배? (correct title + 해요체)
The weather is really nice today.
Please take care of me. / Nice to meet you. (polite 해요체)
Are you busy right now?
I want to learn too.
Did you eat yesterday?
I still don't know very well.
Thanks to you, 선배, I understood. (correct title, 해요체)
Thank you so much for helping me. (correct -셔서 honorific for Seo-yeon, 해요체 final)
Okay I understand!
Shall we have lunch together today?
See you again tomorrow!
선배, what time do you get off work?
What are you eating? (bare -어 ending, casual)
Where are you going? (bare -아 ending)
Help me a bit. (casual imperative -줘)
Okay, got it. (bare -어 ending)
What's wrong? (casual -해 without 요)
I'm hungry. Let's eat together. (-파 and proposal -자, both casual)
Thanks. (casual -워 ending)
How do I do this? (bare -해 without 요)
Hello. I look forward to working with you. (-십니까, -습니다; formal but not offensive with Seo-yeon)
Thank you, 선배님. (-습니다; stiff but acceptable)
Yes, I understand. (-습니다; overly formal)
Thank you for your hard work today. (-습니다; formal; correct -시- for Seo-yeon)
I'm sorry. I made a mistake. (-습니다 formal apology)
What did the team lead say? (should: 팀장님이 뭐라고 하셨어요 — missing 님 and -시-)
Team lead Oh is coming to the meeting. (should: 오 팀장님이 … 오세요 — missing 님 and -시-)
The team lead ate lunch. (먹었어요 → 드셨어요; also missing 님)
I asked the team lead. (한테 → 께; also missing 님 on 팀장)
What is the team lead doing? (should: 팀장님이 뭐 하세요 — missing 님 and -시-)
Did you hear what team lead Oh said? (말 → 말씀; missing 님)
*I'm going to go yesterday. (future tense with past adverb; should be 어제 갔어요)
*I'm learning Korea. (한국 → 한국어; wrong object noun, register fine)
*I arrived so I'll be at the office now. (있을게요 = future intent; should be 있어요 for current state)
*The lunch I eat yesterday was delicious. (present relative clause 먹는 with past anchor; should be 먹은)
*I'm learning Korean since 5 years ago. (present progressive with past anchor; should be 배운 지 5년 됐어요)

text: 선배님 제가 이 파일 보내줄 수 있을게요.
notes: *I will be able to send this file. (수 있을게요 ungrammatical; should be 보내드릴게요 or 보낼 수 있어요)
